name: ALICE Collaboration
notes: CONFLICT/history: the 2008 ALICE detector paper (src:colliders-lhc-alice-detector-jinst-2008) states the collaboration then included 'over 1000 physicists and engineers from 105 Institutes in 30 countries' - the smaller, historical figure at first-collisions time, consistent with a collaboration that grew to ~2000/174/40 by 2022. Both figures are genuine, just from different dates; the more recent (2022) figure is used for the current membership block.

summary.plain: The international team of scientists and engineers who built and run the ALICE experiment. Formed in March 1993 when it submitted its Letter of Intent to CERN, the collaboration has grown to almost 2000 members from around 174 institutes in about 40 countries.
summary.technical: Collaboration operating experiment:alice at CERN LHC Point 2. Formed 1 March 1993 with the submission of the ALICE Letter of Intent to the CERN LHC Committee; approved February 1997. As of April 2022: almost 2000 members, 174 institutes, 40 countries (home.cern), up from 'over 1000 physicists and engineers from 105 Institutes in 30 countries' at the time of the 2008 detector paper.
